cells.tense: You are steady here, at a thing that has not sorted itself into parts, and the steadiness is work.
cells.ask: Show one unfinished piece to someone who has not seen it, and listen to what they say back.
cells.core:
You're at the ground level of something that hasn't separated into parts yet, and you're staying there. Not forcing it into a name, not backing off. Two pulls run in you at once: the wish to grow this out, and how much of it you can actually do today. You hold both without dropping either. That is rarer than it sounds. Neither one has edged the other out.

What you're carrying sits where nothing has divided yet, and your hands stay level on it. When you pass even the rough edge of it to another person, you'll find out which parts already have weight. Letting it be seen is not the end of carrying it. It's the part that only happens once someone else is standing near enough to see.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the wish and the limit, and neither one slips.
cells.verb: Tending what grows, through form, with steady hands
cells.place: at the ground floor of something that has not taken its shape yet

cells.tense: You are already running ahead of something that has not had time to form, bracing for what it will ask of you.
cells.ask: Leave it alone for one day and let it do whatever it does without your hands on it.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of something that hasn't had time to become anything yet. In your head it's further along — already growing, already fragile, already something worth defending — and you're living out there with a version that doesn't exist. You're guarding it from a season that hasn't arrived.

What that costs: you can't see the small thing opening today, because you're already worried about the one after this. Where you're standing, the grip has started to close, and the growing thing can't tell your hand holding it up from your hand holding it shut. Let it be for a day. No checking, no fixing, no measuring how far it has gotten. Whatever still stands tomorrow is yours to keep tending.
cells.sheetLine: Let it stand one day without you in it.
cells.verb: Tending what grows, through form, with steady hands

cells.tense: You stepped away from the work of growing things, and the place you stepped away from is still where you're standing.
cells.ask: Take one small, low-stakes thing and tend it for a day, expecting nothing back from it.
cells.core:
You know how to grow something. You've stepped back from doing it. The door behind you is closed, and you're still facing it, which doesn't leave much attention for the ground in front of you.

The ability didn't leave. What ran out is the moving — doing the next small thing with no promise about how it turns out. So start somewhere small. Pick one low-stakes thing and tend it for a single day. Water it, feed it, sit with it, say the plain true thing about where it actually is. Wanting it doesn't need to come first. Doing the small thing is what starts to fill the day back up. What you tend grows something back toward you too.
cells.sheetLine: Start with something small. Doing it is what refills you.
cells.verb: Tending what grows, through form, with steady hands

cells.tense: You are already at the ground level of something, keeping it alive, and you file it under routine.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you are keeping alive right now, and let them hear you call it yours.
cells.core:
You're at the ground floor of something already. The checking, the keeping-conditions-right, the coming back when nobody asked you to — you do all of it and call it just what the day requires. Nothing to mention. Nobody argued, so the quiet work stays under no name.

The care that shows up at the same small tasks every morning has been running under your hand the whole time. Let some of it reach somebody else. Say it once, plainly: this is what has been kept going. Not an award, not a performance. Saying it out loud is how it becomes real in the room. Once another person has stood on that ground with you, it holds better, and there's less to carry by yourself.
cells.sheetLine: What you keep alive is yours. Say so, once.
cells.verb: Tending what grows, through form, with steady hands
cells.place: at the ground floor of something that has not taken its shape yet

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that working at the ground level itself is the care — that is the model speaking, not something the record shows about this person or their life. The reader could reasonably say the read is wrong because the thing growing under their hands is not really theirs to tend, or the two demands I name are not the two they carry. The ask survives either way, because offering something up for an answer is doable regardless of what the actual form is. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line claiming to know the quiet work they do when no one is watching. Fixed before writing: no claim about what grows, what it costs, or what happened when they handed something over before.
